newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Freed diplomat wants to become Peru hostage again.
newsitem.headline: Freed diplomat wants to become Peru hostage again.

text.p: Guatemala's ambassador to Peru, a former captive of Marxist rebels who are still holding 74 hostages in Lima, wants to return to captivity to help negotiate an end to the crisis, an official said on Friday.
Ambassador Jose Maria Argueta would return "if and only if the government of Peru authorises it," presidential spokesman Ricardo de la Torre told reporters.

De la Torre said Argueta, who was freed by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement rebels on Dec. 26, was brave to offer to return to the Japanese ambassador's home in Peru, where he was taken hostage along with hundreds of others on Dec. 17.
De la Torre said Guatemala's foreign minister had agreed to Argueta's proposal to become a hostage again, but Peru had not authorised any negotiating role for the ambassador.
Argueta stayed in Peru after he was released, declining an invitation to attend a gala ceremony on Dec. 29 for the historic peace accord ending Guatemala's 36-year civil war.
